headline: NEW TARIFFS PROPOSED
dek: The U.S. trade representative proposed tariffs on 14 trading partners after an eight-month Section 301 probe into “excess capacity,” Reuters reports.

items.title: CHINA
items.text: An added 20%, on top of first-term tariffs, kept within the cap of a trade truce that expires Jan. 10, 2027.

items.title: EU · JAPAN · S. KOREA · TAIWAN
items.text: New rates stay within the 15% caps in existing trade deals.

items.title: INDIA · VIETNAM · 7 MORE
items.text: Rates vary. Partners without finalized deals, like India and Vietnam, remain in talks. Malaysia stays within its 19% cap.

items.title: NOT INCLUDED YET
items.text: Mexico and Norway are still under review, the trade office said.

means.label: When:
means.text: A public comment period and hearing come first, which could push the tariffs into January 2027. Rates to be published in the Federal Register.

means.label: The administration:
means.text: Says these partners create “structural excess capacity” that burdens U.S. commerce.

means.label: The pushback:
means.text: China rejected the excess-capacity charge in a July paper. A U.S. official said Washington doesn't expect China to retaliate.

sources: Sources: AP, Nov. 25; Reuters via Investing.com, Nov. 25; BBC, Nov. 25; MOFCOM, July 28; Federal Register 2026-05214.
